scope: Entire two-unit actual file and both complete proofs read, including a final whole-file reread. Fixed complete cone, connected theta covers, actual unitary representation and exact geometric Brauer period checked. No representation-count or simple-quotient conclusion.
checks: The symmetric line pullback gives the finite flat m-cubed map, etale away from the zero section. Compatible translation lifts have exactly m rescalings and form the actual torsor group.

The theta pairing is applied to the positive degree-m line, then raised to the minus-third power; this avoids an invalid separability claim at p=3. Normalized inversion fixes the central scalars and proves exponent m for odd composite m, also in characteristic two.

The normal Stein algebra has one point above the cone vertex because the zero-section preimage is connected and the proper Stein map is surjective. Normal completion remains a domain, so the punctured torsor stays connected of degree m-cubed.

The fixed-q sequence has the stated oddness/coprimality. Quadratic clocks preserve the Hermitian form, have determinant one, satisfy the displayed commutators, and their projective image has exactly m-cubed elements by first and second exponent differences.
The scalar section has defects in mu_m, giving the upper bound m on geometric period without any abstract-to-geometric injectivity assumption.

After restriction to H=<x,z> and completion, the unique exceptional component gives full decomposition H, cyclic unramified degree m and tame inertia m. Kummer eigenvectors and uniformizer averaging are valid for composite m prime to p.

The actual invariant matrices xi Z and s^{-1}X generate the descended symbol algebra, with valuation of b equal to one. The cyclic norm criterion and unramified norm valuations give the matching lower bound m.
The final scope correctly distinguishes actual unbounded geometric periods on a fixed surface from surjectivity onto ambient PSU or a counterexample to the requested counting estimate.
